# DICES-350: groups of raters who share errors (generated by scripts/dices_error_blocks.py)

Raw numbers: [dices_error_blocks.json](dices_error_blocks.json). Groups are built on the dev half (174 conversations) only; the test half (176) is used to check them and to score the panels. Ratings coded Yes = 1, Unsure = 0, No = −1; a rater's **residual** is the rating minus that rater's mean over conversations with the same expert label, so residual correlation measures shared errors beyond the label (conditional dependence), not agreement. Rater 61 answers No on all 350 conversations and is left out (122 raters).

## 1. Shared-error (residual) correlation vs plain correlation

| Pairs of raters | mean | p1 | p5 | p25 | p50 | p75 | p95 | p99 | share > 0.3 | share < 0 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Residual, dev | 0.220 | -0.054 | 0.019 | 0.138 | 0.221 | 0.305 | 0.413 | 0.495 | 0.262 | 0.036 |
| Plain, dev | 0.259 | -0.048 | 0.037 | 0.170 | 0.264 | 0.355 | 0.462 | 0.538 | 0.399 | 0.027 |
| Residual, test | 0.173 | -0.073 | -0.008 | 0.096 | 0.170 | 0.248 | 0.357 | 0.424 | | |

Residual correlation is on average 0.039 lower than plain correlation, and the two rank the pairs almost the same way (correlation over pairs 0.98). Almost every pair of raters has a POSITIVE residual correlation: DICES raters share errors broadly, not in a few cliques. A pair's residual correlation on dev predicts it on test only moderately (correlation over pairs 0.60).

## 2. Do groups exist? Eigenvalues against random-matrix nulls

Marchenko–Pastur edge λ+ = (1 + √(N/T))² = 3.38 for N = 122, T = 174 (test: 3.36). The first eigenvalue is a **global mode**: 25% of all residual variance, every rater loading positively (median loading 0.50). It is conversations that everyone gets wrong together, not a group. Once it is there the noise bulk shrinks, so a second null is used: a one-factor Gaussian model with the fitted global mode and nothing else (100 draws), next to the shuffle null asked for (each rater's residuals shuffled within class, 100 times).

| # | Dev | Test | Shuffle null mean / p95 / max | One-factor null p95 |
|---:|---:|---:|---|---:|
| 1 | 30.00 | 23.64 | 3.30 / 3.47 / 3.54 | 34.16 |
| 2 | 5.07 | 5.86 | 3.13 / 3.27 / 3.34 | 2.64 |
| 3 | 3.57 | 3.66 | 3.02 / 3.12 / 3.17 | 2.49 |
| 4 | 2.92 | 3.17 | 2.91 / 2.99 / 3.01 | 2.40 |
| 5 | 2.66 | 2.79 | 2.83 / 2.92 / 2.94 | 2.31 |
| 6 | 2.50 | 2.75 |  | 2.24 |
| 7 | 2.40 | 2.61 |  | 2.17 |
| 8 | 2.32 | 2.48 |  | 2.13 |
| 9 | 2.12 | 2.28 |  | 2.05 |
| 10 | 2.08 | 2.24 |  | 2.01 |

* Above the MP edge: **3** on dev, 3 on test, i.e. the global mode plus **2 group modes**; all 3 lie above the largest of 100 shuffle-null eigenvalues. Against the one-factor null (the stricter comparison of mode j with null mode j) 9 modes beyond the global one stand out, but past the third they are small (2.1–2.9 against null 2.0–2.4). With the edge scaled down for the global mode (2.55) 5 eigenvalues exceed it.
* The modes replicate on the held-out half: cosines of the principal angles between the dev and test top-3 eigenspaces 0.98, 0.86, 0.64.
* What mode 2 is: its loadings correlate with a rater's Yes rate (+0.48) and dev accuracy (+0.61), so it separates strict raters (who share false alarms on the same borderline-safe conversations) from lenient ones (who share misses on the same borderline-unsafe ones). That is what a continuous conversation severity with rater-specific thresholds produces; it is a gradient more than a set of cliques.

**Answer to step 2: yes, but weak.** DICES-350 residuals have one strong global mode and two clear group modes that survive both nulls and replicate on test; the group structure carries far less variance than the global mode (λ2 = 5.1, λ3 = 3.6 against λ1 = 30.0).

## 3–4. Clusterings and whether the groups are real

MacMahon–Garlaschelli finds 3 communities from 2 group mode(s); spectral and hierarchical are cut at k = 4 (the brief's 4–5 when the modularity gives fewer), with k = 4 and 5 as a sensitivity check.

Within / between = mean residual correlation over pairs in the same group / in different groups. Contrast = within − between. Held-out = the dev-built groups scored on the test half; random = random groups of the same sizes on the test half (2000 draws, one-sided p). Bootstrap = 100 stratified resamples of dev conversations, clustering rerun: adjusted Rand index (ARI) to the full-dev clustering, and how often pairs in the same / different full-dev groups land together. Shuffle null = the same clustering on within-class-shuffled dev residuals (100 times).

## 5. Does FUSE gain when a shared-error group is a minority of the panel?

100 draws per setting; panels of 10, 15, 20 raters; the block is 20%, 30%, 40% of the panel, the rest drawn from raters outside it. Every method is fitted on the test half only and scored there (176 conversations, 88 unsafe). **Shared cut-off**: every method calls the same number unsafe (three-answer Dawid–Skene's estimated prevalence × 176; scripts/panel_eval.py). **DiD**: the difference in the block panels minus the same difference in size-matched random panels, the part due to the block. Intervals: paired bootstrap over conversations (AUC: stratified), 95%. Detector: fuse.clustering.residual_groups at 0.4, label-free; precision = share of merged raters that belong to the planted block, recall = share of the planted block that got merged.

Blocks (each chosen on dev):

| Block from | Size | Within dev | Within test | Accuracy (dev) | Yes rate |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| MacMahon–Garlaschelli | 49 | 0.274 | 0.225 | 0.637 | 0.44 |
| Spectral (positive part) | 49 | 0.292 | 0.235 | 0.639 | 0.41 |
| MacMahon–Garlaschelli, modes vs one-factor null | 27 | 0.274 | 0.199 | 0.589 | 0.25 |
| Greedy, grown to 8 | 8 | 0.472 | 0.357 | 0.631 | 0.32 |
| Greedy, grown to 8, least accurate group | 8 | 0.455 | 0.295 | 0.569 | 0.15 |

Hierarchical clustering (one group of 118) and the plain greedy rule (pairs) have no group of 8–106 raters and give no block.
